question: Uh, what does a replacement SIM set me back if mine got stolen?
expected_answer: A replacement physical SIM costs ₹50, issued at a Sarovan Experience Store with your original ID.

key_facts: ₹50 for a replacement physical SIM

question: Uh, can I just pick up the new SIM at any shop that sells your SIMs?
expected_answer: No. Replacement SIMs are issued only at Sarovan-owned Experience Stores, not at franchise retailers or mobile shops, and the connection holder must come in person with original ID.

key_facts: Replacement SIMs are issued only at Sarovan-owned stores
not at franchise retailers or mobile shops
The connection holder must come in person with original ID
meta.plausible_wrong_answer: Yes, any authorised retailer or mobile shop that sells the operator's SIMs can issue a replacement SIM.

question: If my phone got stolen, could someone run up charges on my SIM?
expected_answer: Yes. Until the SIM is blocked, whoever has it can make calls, use data and receive your OTPs, and the usage is charged to your number, so block it straight away and then get a replacement SIM with the same number.

key_facts: anyone with the SIM can use it and run up charges until it is blocked
block the SIM immediately

question: So, how long until my number's actually working with you after I port it?
expected_answer: Port-ins are completed within 7 working days of KYC verification, because each one is manually checked; your old SIM keeps working until the switch.

key_facts: port-in requests within 7 working days of KYC verification
meta.common_prior: About 2 to 3 working days, the standard mobile number portability timeline.

question: So can I keep my WhatsApp and contacts when I bring my number over to you guys?
expected_answer: Yes. Porting keeps the same mobile number, so WhatsApp carries on working with it, and contacts are stored on your phone or cloud account rather than with the network; just copy any contacts saved on the old SIM to the phone before switching.

key_facts: the number stays the same, so WhatsApp continues
contacts are stored on the phone or cloud, not with the operator

question: I'm flying to Dubai next week, do I need to switch on roaming on my postpaid?
expected_answer: No, international roaming is already switched on by default on every postpaid connection; without a pack, data costs ₹55 per MB, so buy an IR pack or switch roaming off in the app.

key_facts: international roaming is switched on by default on every postpaid connection
data ₹55 per MB
meta.common_prior: Yes, international roaming has to be activated first, in the app or by SMS, before you travel.

question: And the seven-day one, what sort of data allowance comes with that?
expected_answer: The IR 7 days pack costs ₹1,999 and gives 2 GB data, along with 100 minutes of calls and 20 SMS.

history.text: Hi, I'm going to Singapore for a few days next month and I want a roaming pack.
Sure, there are two packs that cover Singapore, a seven-day one and a thirty-day one.

key_facts: IR 7 days, ₹1,999: 2 GB data

question: I'm flying to Dubai next week, is there a charge for calls I receive there?
expected_answer: Yes, usually. Abroad your phone is on a foreign partner network, so an incoming call has to be routed internationally to you and that network bills your home operator; that is why incoming calls are charged while roaming unless a pack includes them.

key_facts: the call is routed internationally to the foreign network
the partner network charges your home operator

question: Why was there a late fee when I paid just one day after the due date?
expected_answer: Since 1 July 2026 there is no grace period on postpaid bills, so a late payment fee of ₹250 is added on the day after the due date if the full amount hasn't been received.

key_facts: There is no grace period
a late payment fee of ₹250 is added on the day after the due date
meta.common_prior: There is usually a grace period of around a week, so paying one day late should not attract a late fee.

question: My bill's overdue and calls are barred, how much do I pay to get reconnected?
expected_answer: No, while services are only barred there is no reconnection fee; pay the full outstanding amount and services are restored within 2 hours. A ₹200 reconnection fee applies only after full disconnection.

key_facts: Reconnection while barred: there is no reconnection fee
services are restored within 2 hours
Reconnection after full disconnection: a reconnection fee of ₹200 applies

question: What's the difference between my bill date and my due date, exactly, on postpaid?
expected_answer: The bill date is when your bill for the cycle is generated; the due date is the last day by which your payment must reach the operator to avoid late charges.
answer_aliases: bill generated vs last day to pay

key_facts: bill date is when the bill is generated
due date is the last day to pay without late charges

question: What does data rollover mean on Flex four ninety-nine, does it keep adding up?
expected_answer: On Flex 499, unused data rolls over to the next bill cycle only; whatever is left of it at the end of that cycle expires, so it does not keep accumulating.

key_facts: unused data rolls over to the next bill cycle only
It does not keep accumulating from month to month
meta.common_prior: Unused data keeps accumulating month after month up to a rollover cap, often around 200 GB.

question: Is Flex five forty-nine the same as four ninety-nine when the data's all used up?
expected_answer: On Flex 549, once the 100 GB plus any rollover is used, speed drops to 1 Mbps with no extra charge, whereas Flex 499 charges ₹10 per GB for extra data.

key_facts: speed is reduced to 1 Mbps for the rest of the bill cycle, with no extra charge
data is charged at ₹10 per GB

question: On my Flex plan, uh, how much data does an hour of HD video take?
expected_answer: Roughly 1 to 3 GB per hour for HD streaming, depending on the app and quality setting; standard definition uses well under 1 GB an hour.
answer_aliases: a couple of gigs an hour

key_facts: roughly 1 to 3 GB per hour in HD

question: I'm on the hundred meg fibre plan, why's it suddenly stuck at like ten megs?
expected_answer: Most likely you've crossed the Fibre 100 fair usage limit of 3,300 GB in this bill cycle, after which speed drops to 10 Mbps until the next bill cycle; a ₹199 top-up restores full speed straight away.

key_facts: fair usage limit of 3,300 GB per bill cycle, after which speed drops to 10 Mbps
₹199 top-up

question: Mostly at night, like every day after nine, why does it get slower then?
expected_answer: Evenings are peak hours: many more people are streaming and gaming, so shared parts of the network and the sites' servers get congested, and neighbours' Wi-Fi adds interference; a wired speed test helps separate network congestion from Wi-Fi problems.

history.text: My home internet's been really sluggish lately.
I've checked, and your line itself looks healthy right now. When do you notice it most?

key_facts: peak-hour congestion when many users are online
Wi-Fi interference can add to it

question: Why did I get charged for the technician who came to fix my Wi-Fi?
expected_answer: A ₹300 visit charge applies when the technician finds the problem is in your own devices, internal wiring, an extender or Wi-Fi settings you changed; visits for faults in our network or fibre line are free.

key_facts: a ₹300 visit charge is added to your next bill
the problem is in your own devices

question: Um, if my router just dies on me, what happens, do you guys replace it?
expected_answer: Only within the 12-month warranty from installation, for hardware faults; after that a replacement router costs ₹1,200 (or you can use your own), and physical, liquid or surge damage is never covered.

key_facts: 12-month warranty from the installation date
a replacement router from Sarovan costs ₹1,200
meta.plausible_wrong_answer: Yes, the router belongs to the provider, so a faulty one is always replaced free of charge.

question: Upstairs in the bedroom, so do I need to use the two point four network there?
expected_answer: Probably yes: the 2.4 GHz band reaches further and passes through walls and floors better, while 5 GHz is faster but has a shorter range, so upstairs the 2.4 GHz network will usually hold a steadier connection.

history.text: The Wi-Fi works fine in the living room where the router is.
Good, that means the connection itself is healthy. Where does it give you trouble?

key_facts: 2.4 GHz has longer range and passes through walls better
5 GHz is faster but shorter range

question: My fibre was dead for most of last week, is there any sort of compensation for that?
expected_answer: Yes, if it was a network fault: an automatic credit of ₹30 per full day beyond the first 48 hours, added to your next bill and capped at ₹600 per bill cycle.

key_facts: automatic credit of ₹30 per full day of outage beyond the first 48 hours
capped at ₹600 per bill cycle
meta.plausible_wrong_answer: Yes, you can ask for a pro-rata refund of the monthly rental for all four days.

question: My fibre was down for hours last week, is there a reason cut cables take so long to fix?
expected_answer: Yes. The technicians first have to find exactly where the cable is broken, often with a fibre tester, may need to dig or get access, and then every hair-thin glass fibre in the cable has to be spliced individually and tested.

key_facts: the break has to be located first
each fibre has to be spliced individually

question: What documents do I need to bring for a new postpaid connection?
expected_answer: Aadhaar biometric e-KYC is enough on its own; without Aadhaar, bring your original passport, voter ID or driving licence plus one passport-size photograph, and a refundable ₹500 security deposit applies.

key_facts: Aadhaar biometric e-KYC is enough on its own
a refundable security deposit of ₹500

question: How many SIMs can I have in my name, like across all the networks?
expected_answer: Under the national rule one person can hold up to nine mobile connections across all operators combined, or six in Jammu and Kashmir, Assam and the North-East.

key_facts: nine connections per person across all operators
six in Jammu and Kashmir, Assam and the North-East

question: And the security amount from when I joined, how does that get handled?
expected_answer: The security deposit is refunded within 45 days of the final bill being paid, and only to your registered bank account; there are no cash refunds.

history.text: I'm moving abroad, so I want to close my postpaid connection.
I can help with that. Your final bill will be generated once the closure goes through.

key_facts: refunded within 45 days of the final bill being paid
only to your registered bank account
meta.common_prior: Within about 7 to 10 working days of closing the connection.

question: If I end my fibre plan after six months, how does that work exactly?
expected_answer: If your installation fee was waived for a 12-month commitment, closing before 12 months means the waived ₹1,000 installation fee is added to your final bill; there is no other exit fee.

key_facts: the waived ₹1,000 installation fee is added to your final bill
There is no other exit fee on Home Fibre

question: If I cancel my postpaid connection, will I still get one more bill after that?
expected_answer: Yes. Postpaid usage is billed after the fact, so a final bill covers the calls, data and rental from your last bill date up to the closure date, plus any pending charges.

key_facts: postpaid is billed in arrears
the final bill covers usage up to the closure date

question: Are your stores open on Sundays, and like, until when exactly?
expected_answer: Yes, Sarovan Experience Stores are open on Sunday from 11 am to 6 pm; Monday to Saturday they're open 10 am to 8:30 pm.

key_facts: Sunday 11 am to 6 pm

question: Do I need a special phone for eSIM, or does any phone work?
expected_answer: You need a phone that supports eSIM, because the SIM is built into the handset and the profile is downloaded digitally; most recent mid-range and flagship phones support it, but many older or budget models do not, so check the settings or the model's specs.

key_facts: the phone must support eSIM
many older or budget phones do not

question: I complained about my bill over a week ago, how do I escalate it now?
expected_answer: Since it's not resolved within 7 days, file an appeal with the Sarovan Appellate Authority through the appeal form in the app or at a Sarovan Experience Store, quoting your docket number; appeals are decided within 30 days.

key_facts: if your complaint is not resolved within 7 days
an appeal with the Sarovan Appellate Authority
decided within 30 days

question: I complained about spam calls a week ago, how do I actually stop them?
expected_answer: Register your number on the national Do Not Disturb registry by calling or texting 1909, report spam calls and texts to 1909, and turn on your phone's spam call filtering.

key_facts: register on the Do Not Disturb (DND) registry via 1909
report spam calls to 1909
